title: Central Bank of Nigeria Revised Guidelines on Supervisory Review Process of ICAAP (SRP/ICAAP), September 2021
first_as_of_note: The Guidelines carry an issue month (September 2021) but no stated commencement date; the first annual report is taken to be the one as at 31 December 2021 (¶51 reports as at 31 December). Confirm with the CBN before relying on pre-2022 cycles.

documents.title: Revised Guidelines on Supervisory Review Process of Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (SRP/ICAAP)

related_instruments.title: CBN Guidelines on Stress Testing for the Nigerian Banks
Framework for Regulation and Supervision of Domestic Systemically Important Banks

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guidance: Summary of the ICAAP report: key features, risk exposures and the capital judged adequate (CBN SRP/ICAAP ¶10, ¶4).

requirements.text: Summarise the key features of the ICAAP, the material risk exposures and the level of capital the bank considers adequate to support them.
State the outcome of the independent, complete and forward-looking assessment of the risks the bank is exposed to.
State the internal capital requirement and explain how it reflects the risk profile, business strategy and risk acceptance level.
Show that capital levels are adequate and consistent with the strategy, business plan, risk profile and operating environment on a going-concern basis.

sections.title: Structure and Operations
sections.guidance: Legal and operational structure, business model and where risks arise within the bank and group (¶17, ¶21; Annex B §4).

requirements.text: Prepare the ICAAP at both solo and consolidated level where the bank has subsidiaries.
Identify where risks arise across operating units, the enterprise, the group and external counterparties, so that entity-level capital covers the risks each significant legal entity faces.
Describe the current business model: core business lines, markets, geographies, subsidiaries and products.
Describe the main income and cost drivers, allocated to core business lines, markets, geographies and subsidiaries.
Describe the changes the bank plans to make to its business model and underlying activities.
Explain how the business strategy and the ICAAP are linked.

sections.title: Governance Structure
sections.guidance: Board and senior management responsibilities, organisation and controls around the ICAAP (¶7, ¶9, ¶40–42; Annex B §3).

requirements.text: Show that the Board owns the ICAAP: its design and organisation in line with risk appetite, its implementation and annual update, and the internal capital calculation.
Describe the governance, organisational framework, lines of responsibility and internal controls on which the ICAAP relies.
Show that the Board maintains an appropriate level and quality of capital and understands the nature and materiality of the bank's risks.
Describe the Board framework for assessing risks, relating risk to capital and monitoring compliance with internal policies and regulatory capital limits.
Show that the Board approved the risk appetite and capital management frameworks and oversees how senior management discharges its ICAAP responsibilities.
Describe the process for preparing and updating the ICAAP.
Describe the process for reviewing the ICAAP.
Define the roles and functions of the Board and senior management bodies in the ICAAP.
Define the roles and functions of corporate functions in the ICAAP, such as internal audit, compliance and risk management.
Describe the organisational and contractual safeguards over any outsourced element of the ICAAP.
Describe the internal policies and procedures relevant to the ICAAP.
Provide minutes of Board and relevant committee meetings evidencing implementation of the ICAAP.
Evidence discussion of changes in the risk and capital situation and limit breaches, including decisions on management actions or explicit decisions not to act.
Record decisions on management actions related to internal capital estimates, their aggregation and their comparison with available internal capital, now and forward-looking.

sections.title: Risk Appetite Framework
sections.guidance: The Board-approved risk appetite framework and its use (¶42; Annex B §5).

requirements.text: Provide a copy of the Board-approved risk appetite statement.
Describe how the strategy and business model align with the risk appetite framework.
Describe the process, governance arrangements and Board and senior management roles for designing and implementing the risk appetite framework.
Describe appetite and tolerance levels, thresholds and limits for the material risks, their time horizons and how they are reviewed and updated.
Describe the limit allocation framework within the banking group.
Describe how the risk appetite framework is integrated into and used in risk and overall management.

sections.title: Risk Identification and Materiality Assessment
sections.guidance: How risks are identified, defined and assessed for materiality (¶19–27; Annex B §6).

requirements.text: Identify the risks the bank is exposed to independently, considering its operations and the markets in which it operates.
Consider at least every risk listed in Annex A, treating the list as non-exhaustive.
Base risk identification and materiality on a comprehensive assessment of existing and potential risk factors, including the external environment.
Define the risk identification process, its review frequency and the departments responsible.
Show that all relevant departments take part, with an anchor function (normally risk) coordinating, collating and communicating the risks identified.
Identify all risks, material or not, and state the materiality criteria with their quantitative and qualitative thresholds.
Give internal definitions of the risks the bank is exposed to.
Review materiality continuously in the light of market conditions, counterparty information and possible impact on earnings, capital and reputation.
Describe the approach to identifying risks, the risks identified within each category and the approach to assessing materiality.
Describe the ICAAP time horizon(s), explaining any differences across risk categories and subsidiaries.
Describe the risk categories and sub-categories covered, with their definitions.
Explain any difference between the risks covered by the ICAAP and those covered by the risk appetite framework.
Describe deviations in the ICAAP process and key assumptions across the group and its subsidiaries.
For every measurable risk category, describe the main risk control and mitigation instruments.
Describe the systems for controlling and mitigating non-measurable risks.

sections.title: Risk Assessment and Capital Adequacy
sections.guidance: Quantification of Pillar 2 capital and the assessment of capital adequacy (¶12–13, ¶28–35; Annex B §7).

requirements.text: Assess every risk the bank is or may be exposed to, including risks not captured by Pillar 1.
For risks other than credit, market and operational, state which are quantified for internal capital and which are addressed by controls and mitigation.
Describe the risk measurement and modelling that produce loss and resource estimates, and the reporting to the Board and senior management.
Show the policies and processes that identify, measure and report material risks and relate capital adequacy to risk and to strategy.
Quantify every material risk with methods suited to the bank's organisation and operations.
Use the Pillar 1 methods as the starting point for credit, counterparty, market and operational risk.
Relate capital to risk considering peer and regulatory ratio comparisons, severe adverse events and planned changes to the business.
Apply the CBN guidelines on individual Pillar 2 risks when assessing and quantifying them.
Describe the quantification methods and models for every risk category, with their metrics, assumptions and parameters.
Describe the quality of internal challenge of the internal capital estimates.
Demonstrate that the internal capital estimates are reasonable for the bank's risk profile.
Describe the data used, including subsidiary scope and the length of the time series.
Describe the main differences between the ICAAP methods and those used for the minimum capital adequacy ratio.
Report the internal capital estimate for every material risk category, risk by risk.
Where a risk is material but attracts zero capital, demonstrate the basis for that judgement.

sections.title: Stress Testing
sections.guidance: Stress testing of internal capital and the management actions it triggers (¶36–39, ¶55(c); Annex B §9).

requirements.text: Stress test the risk mitigation and control systems and the adequacy of internal capital.
Apply the CBN stress testing guidelines and assess the relevance of the CBN scenarios and suggested risk drivers to the bank's own drivers.
Articulate realistic management actions for when a severe but plausible scenario takes capital adequacy below the regulatory threshold or below the internal target.
Show management actions are feasible in adverse conditions, considering reputation, preconditions such as covenants and legal constraints, and the effect on the business model.
Quantify the impact of management actions on projected metrics by scenario and evidence similar actions taken in the past, for example through Board minutes.
Show that scenario choice and severity reflect the examiners' view of the bank's risk profile.
Describe the adverse scenarios, their assumptions and key macroeconomic variables.
Describe how reverse stress tests were used to calibrate scenario severity.
Describe the governance of the end-to-end stress testing process and its data infrastructure.
Explain the role of stress test outputs in management decision-making.
Describe key scenario assumptions, including management actions, balance-sheet assumptions, reference dates and horizons.
Report the quantitative outcomes and their impact on profit and loss, internal and regulatory capital, prudential ratios and liquidity.
Explain how the outcomes relate to the business model, strategy, material risks and group entities in scope.

sections.title: Capital Planning
sections.guidance: Strategy, forecasting horizon and the capital plan (¶44; Annex B §2 and the capital-planning item printed as §6 on p. 20).

requirements.text: Describe the business plan and annual budgets, the schedule for reviewing them and the extraordinary events that would trigger a review.
Reconcile the time horizon of the business plan with that of the capital plan.
Describe ordinary and extraordinary sources of capital.
Describe capital planning, including the dimensions considered, time horizons, capital instruments and capital measures.
Describe the main assumptions underlying the capital plan.
Describe the current conclusions of capital planning, such as planned issuances, dividend policy and planned balance-sheet changes.
Provide the documented capital policy and show that capital planning covers every material risk type.
Describe the management framework for preserving capital.
Monitor actual performance against approved capital targets that are commensurate with the risk profile and control environment.

sections.title: Capital Allocation and Reconciliation of Internal Capital
sections.guidance: Allocation of internal capital and its reconciliation with regulatory requirements and capital (¶34; Annex B §8).

requirements.text: Reconcile total internal capital with eligible regulatory capital and explain any instrument included that is not eligible as regulatory capital.
Describe the method and assumptions for allocating internal capital to operating units, subsidiaries, business segments and products.
Describe how internal capital estimates are monitored against allocated capital, including escalation.
State the internal capital available to date, broken down by capital element.
State the internal capital actually allocated to risks, subsidiaries and core business lines.
Compare actual internal capital usage with allocations and explain any case close to or above the allocation.
Reconcile total internal capital with regulatory requirements.
List and define the capital components covering internal capital.
State the supervisory eligibility of each component and explain the inclusion of any ineligible component.

sections.title: Internal Audit and Review of ICAAP
sections.guidance: Independent internal review and audit of the ICAAP (¶8, ¶44–48; Annex B §10).

requirements.text: Subject the ICAAP to independent internal review.
Maintain internal controls, independent reviews and audits over the adequacy, effectiveness and reliability of the ICAAP and the capital planning process.
Review periodically the ICAAP's appropriateness, large exposures and concentrations, data accuracy, scenario validity and stress testing assumptions.
Carry out independent reviews and audits at least as often as the governed interval of {param:icaap_independent_review_max_months} months.
Cover in the periodic review the risk appetite and capital planning, third-party inputs and models, concentration methods, data completeness, scenarios and stress and capital assumptions.
Describe the scope and frequency of the internal audit review of the ICAAP.
Describe the resourcing and independence of the internal audit function.
Describe how open audit issues are tracked and how management action is verified before closure.
Describe the approach to reviewing methods, techniques, assumptions and information sources used in the ICAAP.
Report the outcome of independent validation of risk measurement models.

sections.title: Approval, Review, and Use of ICAAP
sections.guidance: Approval, submission, updating and use of the ICAAP, including its interaction with supervision, the ILAAP and the RRP (¶11, ¶43, ¶50–56; Annex B §12).

requirements.text: Show that the capital process is formalised and documented, subject to internal review and approval by Board and management, and proportionate to the business.
Submit the report with the relevant Board resolutions and senior management reports containing their comments on the ICAAP.
Update and document the ICAAP for material changes in strategy or macroeconomic conditions, and at least once every {param:icaap_review_max_months} months.
Where the CBN requires an updated ICAAP, prepare it in response to that request.
Articulate how examiners' risk-based supervision assessment of inherent risk, risk management quality, direction and net risk is reflected in the ICAAP.
Take into account the examiners' findings from the most recent risk-based examination and demonstrate compliance with their recommendations.
Show consistency between the ICAAP, the ILAAP and the recovery and resolution plan in assumptions, early-warning indicators, triggers, escalation and management actions.
Monitor and report material risks and their effect on capital, the sensitivity of key assumptions, capital sufficiency and future capital requirements.
Document the decisions approved by senior management.
Record the criteria behind key capital decisions: the risk appetite statement, capital allocation, capital adequacy under stress and risk-adjusted performance.

sections.title: Challenges and Further Steps
sections.guidance: Self-assessment, deficiencies and planned improvements (¶10; Annex B §11).

requirements.text: Give a self-assessment of the ICAAP, including areas for improvement, deficiencies in the process and the corrective measures to be taken.
Identify the areas of the ICAAP that need improvement.
Set out the planned capital or organisational actions.

sections.title: Summary of Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process
sections.guidance: Summary of the ICAAP process as a whole, its features and proportionality (¶3–4, ¶14–16, ¶18).

requirements.text: Summarise how the ICAAP covers Board and senior management oversight, policies and limits, capital assessment and planning, risk assessment, stress testing, monitoring and internal control review.
Explain why the approach chosen is proportionate to the size, nature, scale and complexity of the bank's activities.

sections.title: Use of Internal Models for Capital Assessment
sections.guidance: Internal models used to assess capital (¶32; Annex B §7(e), §10(e)).

requirements.text: Where internal models quantify Pillar 2 capital, demonstrate they are appropriate for the bank's risks and exposures and subject to rigorous ongoing validation.
Explain how internal model outputs differ from the regulatory minimum capital measures.
Report the outcome of the independent validation of the models used.

risk_categories.title: Interest rate risk in the banking book
Other material risks (the Annex A list is not exhaustive)

attachments.title: Senior management reports with their comments on the ICAAP
Minutes of Board and committee meetings evidencing implementation of the ICAAP
Evidence of management actions taken in similar past circumstances
CBN request for an updated ICAAP
Source evidence for a manually entered table

stages.title: Board Risk Committee challenge and approval
Board approval (signature on the frozen report)

materiality_matrix.note: The CBN Guideline prescribes no scoring matrix; banks must state their own materiality criteria and thresholds (¶25). This is the platform starting point, adjusted by the bank in P2.

notes.text: Minimum report content may be provided in the ICAAP report itself or as a supplementary submission.
Annex B prints the heading number 6 twice: Risk Identification and Materiality Assessment (p. 19) and Capital planning (p. 20). Citations to the second use the ref AnnexB-6p20.
The CBN challenges the bank's Pillar 2 estimate and may impose a higher Pillar 2 requirement; supervisory add-ons are recorded separately from the bank's own estimate.
The Guidelines contain no requirement to publish ICAAP results, so this framework declares no disclosure specification.
No CBN ICAAP return is registered yet; cycles support drafting, readiness and draft exports, and freeze refuses until a return family for this regulator exists.
Liquidity is assessed in the separate ILAAP; the ICAAP must show consistency with the ILAAP and the recovery plan.
